issues.legal_issue: A government may not demand further contract payments or forfeit a contractor’s deposits when the contractor cannot begin the contracted work because the government has not made the work area accessible or obtained necessary departmental clearance.
material_facts: The contractors obtained contracts to extract sand from riverbed areas and deposited advance contract amounts and security.
The contractors repeatedly sought possession of the areas and clearance from the flood-control department, including before executing the contracts.
The department did not provide the requested clearance or deliver possession, and the contractors extracted no sand.
The government demanded further contract payments and terminated the contracts, forfeiting the deposits.
The contractors were ready and willing to perform, and the court found no fault on their part.
issues.conclusion: The government was not entitled to forfeit any amount or demand further payment under the contracts, and it was directed to refund the deposited amounts.
issues.legal_principle: Where the contractor is not at fault and performance is made infeasible because the government does not provide access or necessary clearance, the government cannot forfeit the contractor’s deposits or demand further contract payments. The court held that Rule 61 of the Punjab Minor Mineral Concession Rules, 1964 and Clause 26 of the agreement did not apply in these circumstances. Although Rule 33 addressed execution of the agreement and forfeiture for failure to execute it, and Rule 59 addressed commencement of the contract period, neither justified recovery or forfeiture on these facts. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: mineral_lease_contract_dispute and contractor_sought_access_and_clearance and government_did_not_provide_access_or_clearance and no_work_was_performed and contractor_was_ready_to_perform

predicates.mineral_lease_contract_dispute: The dispute concerned a government contract granting a contractor rights to extract a mineral.
predicates.contractor_sought_access_and_clearance: The contractor repeatedly asked the responsible authorities for access to the work area and any clearance needed to begin the work.
predicates.government_did_not_provide_access_or_cle: The government did not deliver access to the work area or provide the requested departmental clearance.
predicates.no_work_was_performed: The contractor performed none of the contracted extraction work.
predicates.contractor_was_ready_to_perform: The contractor had deposited contract amounts and remained willing to perform the contract.

issues.definition: When a mineral-contract dispute involves a contractor who sought access and clearance, the government did not provide them, no work was performed, and the contractor remained ready to perform, the government cannot demand further payment or forfeit deposits and must refund the deposits.
